prime_award_base_transaction_description: ELECTRICAL INFRASTRUCTURE STUDY FOR URBAN AIR MOBILITY AIRCRAFT. THE CONVERGENCE OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES, SUCH AS ELECTRIC PROPULSION, AUTONOMY, AND NEW BUSINESS MODELS, SUCH AS APP-BASED RIDE SHARING, ARE GENERATING THE POTENTIAL FOR A NEW AVIATION MARKET KNOWN AS URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM) TO EMERGE. IT IS ENVISIONED THAT UAM MAY REVOLUTIONIZE MOBILITY WITHIN METROPOLITAN AREAS BY ENABLING A SAFE, EFFICIENT, CONVENIENT, AFFORDABLE, AND ACCESSIBLE AIR TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM FOR PASSENGERS AND CARGO. SUCH AN AIR TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM COULD BRING AVIATION INTO PEOPLE S DAILY LIVES AND PROVIDE AN AUGMENTATION AND/OR ALTERNATIVE TO OTHER GROUND-BASED TRANSIT MODES, SUCH AS CARS. BECAUSE UAM IS ENVISIONED TO AID IN MOBILITY AROUND DENSE URBAN AREAS WHERE LAND AVAILABILITY IS SCARCE, MOST VEHICLES BEING PROPOSED IN THIS SPACE ARE CAPABLE OF VERTICAL TAKEOFF AND LANDING (VTOL) LIKE CONVENTIONAL HELICOPTERS. ADDITIONALLY, THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ELECTRIC PROPULSION ONTO SMALL VTOL AIRCRAFT MAY ENABLE MORE EFFICIENT, QUIETER, AND FASTER VEHICLES THAN ARE ACHIEVABLE WITH CONVENTIONAL PROPULSION SYSTEMS AND CONFIGURATIONS. THEREFORE, THE VEHICLES THAT ARE LIKELY TO PERFORM UAM MISSIONS HAVE BECOME KNOWN AS ELECTRIC VERTICAL TAKEOFF AND LANDING, OR EVTOL, VEHICLES. THE LOCATIONS FROM WHICH THESE UAM AIRCRAFT WILL OPERATE HAVE BEEN TERMED  VERTIPORTS.  EACH VERTIPORT MAY HAVE A SINGLE  VERTIPAD  OR MULTIPLE VERTIPADS FROM WHICH AIRCRAFT MAY TAKEOFF, LAND, PARK, AND/OR RECHARGE. THE EXACT DISTRIBUTION, NUMBER, AND SIZE OF VERTIPORTS ACROSS A METROPOLITAN AREA IS AS YET UNDEFINED, THOUGH SOME ESTIMATES HAVE BEEN PRESENTED BY NASA-FUNDED RESEARCH1 AND UBER.2 FOR THIS INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT PURELY ELECTRIC VTOL AIRCRAFT, THERE WILL NEED TO BE RECHARGING CAPABILITIES AT MANY, IF NOT ALL, OF THE VERTIPORTS. SUCH INFRASTRUCTURE DOES NOT EXIST TODAY AND MUST BE INSTALLED PRIOR TO AN ALL-ELECTRIC UAM NETWORK BEING IMPLEMENTED.   THE PURPOSE OF THIS TASK IS TO HELP PROVIDE A HIGH-LEVEL UNDERSTANDING OF THE CHANGES THAT NEED TO BE MADE TO THE EXISTING ELECTRIC GRID TO SUPPORT EVTOL OPERATIONS AS A PART OF A UAM TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM. IN ADDITION TO A QUALITATIVE DISCUSSION OF THESE NEEDED MODIFICATIONS ESTIMATES OF THE TIMEFRAMES AND COSTS REQUIRED TO DEVELOP INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING ALL INFRASTRUCTURE ELEMENTS FROM THE ELECTRICITY GENERATION THROUGH TO THE CHARGING OF THE AIRCRAFT AT A VERTIPORT, WILL BE THE MAIN OUTPUT OF THIS TASK.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: INVESTIGATION OF SHORT TAKE-OFF AND LANDING (STOL) APPLICABILITY TO URBAN, SUBURBAN, AND RURAL AIR MOBILITY. RISING POPULATIONS IN AND AROUND CITIES WORLDWIDE ARE CAUSING SUBSTANTIAL MOBILITY ISSUES. THERE IS INCREASING GEOGRAPHICAL SPRAWL OF URBAN AREAS AND COMMUTE TIMES ARE EVER-RISING, BOTH DUE TO INCREASING COMMUTING DISTANCES AND INCREASING CONGESTION ON ROADS AND PUBLIC TRANSIT. MEANWHILE, A CONVERGENCE OF EVOLVING TECHNOLOGIES, SUCH AS ELECTRIC PROPULSION AND AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS, IS ENABLING TRANSFORMATIONAL CHANGES IN AIRCRAFT DESIGN AND OPERATION. THERE IS INTEREST, THEREFORE, IN EXPANDING THE METROPOLITAN TRANSPORT NETWORK INTO THE AIR.  AT PRESENT, THERE IS SUBSTANTIAL INTEREST IN THE USE OF ELECTRIC VERTICAL TAKE-OFF AND LANDING (EVTOL) AIRCRAFT FOR URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM); HOWEVER, THIS CONCEPT HAS MANY TECHNOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CHALLENGES. OPERATION IN A COMPLETELY  URBAN ENVIRONMENT IS A STEP CHANGE FROM TODAYS AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS IN WHICH WE ATTEMPT TO SEPARATE AIR TRAVEL FROM POPULOUS AREAS. THE USE OF EVTOL AIRCRAFT THEMSELVES ALSO INTRODUCES A NUMBER OF INHERENT CONSTRAINTS TO VEHICLE AND MISSION DESIGN, SUCH AS HIGH ENERGY AND POWER REQUIREMENTS DUE TO VERTICAL FLIGHT, AND LIMITED FORECASTED BATTERY TECHNOLOGIES. AN ALTERNATIVE POSSIBILITY WOULD BE TO USE SHORT TAKE-OFF AND LANDING (STOL) AIRCRAFT. STOL OPERATIONS, WITH NO HOVER REQUIREMENT, INHERENTLY HAVE REDUCED ENERGY AND POWER REQUIREMENTS RELATIVE TO VERTICAL OPERATIONS. IF A VIABLE CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS EXISTS FOR STOL, INCLUDING ELECTRIC STOL (ESTOL) AIRCRAFT, THERE MAY BE IMPROVEMENTS RELATIVE TO EVTOL OPERATIONS, IN ASPECTS SUCH AS ENERGY EFFICIENCY, RANGE, PAYLOAD CAPACITY, OVERALL VEHICLE PERFORMANCE, NOISE, AND INFRASTRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS. FOR EXAMPLE, WITH A GREATER RANGE THAN EVTOL OPERATIONS, STOL OPERATIONS MAY IMPROVE THE ACCESS OF SUBURBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES TO URBAN CENTERS, PROVIDE ACCESS TO IMPROVED WORK AND STUDY OPPORTUNITIES, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVE THE ECONOMY IN RURAL, SUBURBAN, AND URBAN AREAS. IN ADDITION, THERE ARE HAVE BEEN MANY STOL AIRCRAFT DESIGNED AND BUILT IN THE PAST, AND NOVEL ESTOL AIRCRAFT SHOULD BE ABLE TO BE CERTIFIED MORE EASILY UNDER PART 23 AMENDMENT 64 THAN EVTOL AIRCRAFT. STOL VEHICLES COULD BE EARLY ADOPTERS OF TECHNOLOGICAL IMPROVEMENTS, SUCH AS BATTERIES AND AUTONOMY, AND COULD ENABLE MANY OF THE CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS NEW TECHNOLOGY TO BE PROVEN AHEAD OF USE IN EVTOL AIRCRAFT.  ONE IMMEDIATELY OBVIOUS CHALLENGE WITH STOL OPERATIONS IN AN URBAN ENVIRONMENT IS THE LARGER GROUND FOOTPRINT, BOTH IN TERMS OF THE RUNWAY REQUIRED AND THE APPROACH AND DEPARTURE PATHS CLOSE TO THE GROUND. THIS MAY BE LESS OF A CONCERN IN SUBURBAN AND RURAL AREAS. ANOTHER CHALLENGE IS THAT STOL OPERATIONS ARE LIKELY TO BE MORE SUSCEPTIBLE TO VARIATION IN WIND DIRECTION THAN VTOL OPERATIONS. THIS STATEMENT OF WORK SEEKS TO INVESTIGATE THE APPLICABILITY OF STOL OPERATIONS TO URBAN, SUBURBAN AND RURAL ENVIRONMENTS.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: IMPACT OF AUTONOMOUS GROUND VEHICLES ON URBAN AIR MOBILITY OPERATIONS. OVER THE PAST FEW YEARS THE CONCEPT OF UTILIZING ADVANCED, SMALL AIRCRAFT FOR ON-DEMAND TRANSPORTATION AROUND METROPOLITAN AREAS HAS BEEN GROWING IN POPULARITY. SUCH NOVEL TRANSPORTATION SERVICES FOR BOTH PEOPLE AND GOODS HAS BECOME KNOWN AS URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM). ADVANCES IN ELECTRIC PROPULSION SYSTEMS, AUTOMATION/AUTONOMY, MANUFACTURING, AND OTHER TECHNOLOGIES MAY CONVERGE TO PROVIDE NOVEL AIRCRAFT CONFIGURATIONS THAT ARE AFFORDABLE, SAFE, AND QUIET ENOUGH TO OPERATE AS A PRACTICAL MEANS OF DAILY TRANSPORTATION. IN 2016, THE RIDE HAILING COMPANY UBER RELEASED A WHITE PAPER DESCRIBING ITS PLANS TO BEGIN OFFERING AN URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM) SERVICE WITH THE NOVEL ELECTRIC VERTICAL TAKEOFF AND LANDING (I.E., EVTOL) AIRCRAFT, AND SEVERAL MANUFACTURERS HAVE SINCE MADE PUBLIC THEIR PLANS OF DEVELOPING EVTOL AIRCRAFT TO OPERATE WITHIN SUCH A SYSTEM.  THE UAM CONCEPT SHARES SOME SIMILARITIES WITH EXISTING PUBLIC TRANSIT SYSTEMS. SPECIFICALLY, MOST UAM CONCEPTS RELY ON PASSENGERS TO CHANGE MODES TO COMPLETE A SINGLE TRIP I.E., A TRAVELER WILL TAKE A GROUND VEHICLE OR WALK TO A TAKEOFF LOCATION, EXIT THE GROUND VEHICLE (IF REQUIRED), TRANSFER INTO AN AIR VEHICLE, THEN TRANSFER AGAIN AFTER A FLIGHT TO A GROUND-BASED TRANSPORTATION MODE. SUCH MULTI-MODE TRIPS ARE COMMON TODAY WITH TRANSIT SYSTEMS WITH THE AIR PORTION OF THE TRIP BEING REPLACED BY A GROUND-BASED MODE (OR MODES) USING BUSES AND/OR TRAINS. THEREFORE, THE LESSONS LEARNED FROM THE TRANSIT WORLD MAY BE DIRECTLY APPLICABLE TO UAM OPERATIONS, AND COULD HELP INCREASE PUBLIC ADOPTION OF UAM TRANSPORTATION. FOR EXAMPLE, TRANSIT RIDERS MAY PREFER TO HAVE SERVICES, SUCH AS THE DRY CLEANERS, CO-LOCATED WITH A TRANSIT STATION SO THAT THEY DO NOT NEED TO MAKE AN EXTRA TRIP. SUCH PREVIOUSLY EVIDENCED BEHAVIOR MAY IMPLY THAT UAM OPERATIONS SHOULD CONSIDER CO-LOCATING THESE SERVICES AT THE AIR VEHICLE TAKEOFF AND LANDING LOCATIONS. AT THE SAME TIME AS THE UAM CONCEPT IS GROWING IN POPULARITY, THERE ARE RAPID DEVELOPMENTS IN AUTOMATING GROUND VEHICLES. COMPANIES SUCH AS WAYMO (AND MANY OTHERS) ARE WORKING TO DEVELOP SELF-DRIVING OR AUTONOMOUS CARS THAT MAY ONE DAY BE CAPABLE OF SAFELY AND CONSISTENTLY TRANSPORTING PEOPLE WITHOUT THE NEED FOR HUMAN DRIVERS. THERE ARE MULTIPLE VISIONS FOR HOW AUTONOMOUS GROUND VEHICLES WILL ENTER THE MARKETPLACE. SOME ARE CONSIDERING PERSONAL OWNERSHIP MODELS SIMILAR TO HOW MANY CARS TODAY ARE PRIVATELY OWNED BY THE INDIVIDUALS WHO USE THEM FOR TRANSPORTATION. OTHERS ARE CONSIDERING PROVIDING AN ON-DEMAND SERVICE IN WHICH INDIVIDUALS REQUEST RIDES FROM A COMPANY WHO OPERATES A FLEET OF VEHICLES. SUCH ON-DEMAND SERVICES ARE SIMILAR TO EXISTING RIDE-HAILING SERVICES FROM THE END USER S PERSPECTIVE AND MAY ALLOW USERS TO SHARE RIDES OR RIDE ALONE. CONSUMER PREFERENCES RELATED TO ISSUES SUCH AS PRIVACY WHILE TRAVELING AND THE ABILITY TO OWN AND CUSTOMIZE THEIR VEHICLE WILL DICTATE WHICH OF THESE OPERATIONAL MODELS BECOMES MORE DOMINANT IN THE MARKETPLACE.  REGARDLESS OF THE OPERATIONAL MODEL, AUTONOMOUS CARS MAY ALLOW PASSENGERS TO BE PRODUCTIVE WHILE TRAVELING (E.G., CHECKING EMAIL OR WORKING IN OTHER WAYS) OR TO RELAX (E.G., READ A BOOK, WATCH A SHOW), BOTH OF WHICH MAY INCREASE THE WILLINGNESS OF INDIVIDUALS TO TRAVEL BY CAR AROUND METROPOLITAN AREAS AND DECREASE THE IMPORTANCE OF HAVING  SHORT  COMMUTING TIMES. ADDITIONALLY, ONCE AUTONOMOUS CARS ARE A SIGNIFICANT FRACTION OF ALL GROUND TRAFFIC, THEY MAY REDUCE SOME EXISTING PROBLEMS, SUCH AS TRAFFIC JAMS, AND INCREASE THE SPEEDS AT WHICH GROUND VEHICLES CAN SAFELY OPERATE, WHICH CAN REDUCE TRAVEL TIMES BY GROUND. SUCH CHANGES IN CONSUMER PREFERENCE OR THE MANNER IN WHICH GROUND VEHICLES OPERATE MAY HAVE AN ADVERSE IMPACT ON ONE OF THE PRIMARY BENEFITS OF THE UAM CONCEPT THE ABILITY OF UAM TO SAVE TRAVELERS TIME. ALTERNATIVELY, THE PROLIFERATION OF AUTONOMOUS GROUND VEHICLES MAY PROVIDE SOME BENEFITS TO UAM SERVICES.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: EXPLORATION OF POTENTIAL MINIMUM VIABLE PRODUCT MISSIONS FOR PASSENGER-CARRYING URBAN AIR MOBILITY MISSIONS. THE CONVERGENCE OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES, SUCH AS ELECTRIC PROPULSION, AUTONOMY, AND NEW BUSINESS MODELS, SUCH AS APP-BASED RIDE SHARING, ARE GENERATING THE POTENTIAL FOR A NEW AVIATION MARKET KNOWN AS URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM) TO EMERGE. IT IS ENVISIONED THAT UAM MAY REVOLUTIONIZE MOBILITY WITHIN METROPOLITAN AREAS BY ENABLING A SAFE, EFFICIENT, CONVENIENT, AFFORDABLE, AND ACCESSIBLE AIR TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM FOR PASSENGERS AND CARGO. SUCH AN AIR TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM COULD BRING AVIATION INTO PEOPLE S DAILY LIVES AND PROVIDE AN AUGMENTATION AND/OR ALTERNATIVE TO OTHER GROUND-BASED TRANSIT MODES, SUCH AS CARS. THE UAM MARKET IS NOT LIKELY TO APPEAR OVERNIGHT. RATHER, SOME FORM OF EVOLUTIONARY APPROACH BASED ON THE PACE OF TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT, SOCIETAL ACCEPTANCE, AND MANY OTHER FACTORS MAY BRING US FROM THE CURRENT STATE OF THE ART TO THE ENVISIONED FUTURE STATE WHERE AVIATION IS A NORMAL PART OF PEOPLE S DAILY LIVES. TO HELP NASA ARMD CONSIDER POTENTIAL EVOLUTIONARY PATHS TO PASSENGER-CARRYING UAM OPERATIONS, THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MINIMUM VIABLE PRODUCT IS THE FOCUS OF THIS TASK. MINIMUM VIABLE PRODUCT (MVP) IS A TERM THAT EVOLVED FROM PRODUCT DEVELOPERS IN SILICON VALLEY WHO WERE SEEKING WAYS TO GET PRODUCTS INTO THE HANDS OF CONSUMERS AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE. BY DEFINING THE SMALLEST SET OF FEATURES THAT SATISFIES EARLY ADOPTERS, THE MVP APPROACH OFFERS THE ADVANTAGE OF PURSUING AN AMBITIOUS VISION WHILE LEARNING FROM REAL-WORLD USERS, GENERATING REVENUE EARLIER IN THE PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT PROCESS (POSSIBLY), AND FEEDING THE BUILD-MEASURE-LEARN CYCLE WITH DATA. MVP IS AN ITERATIVE PROCESS THAT REDUCES THE RISK OF DEVELOPING A PRODUCT BASED ON RISKY ASSUMPTIONS. THERE ARE MANY POTENTIAL MISSIONS THAT COULD EMERGE AS A MVP. ONE POTENTIAL MISSION, WHICH HAS RECEIVED SOME ATTENTION IN THE LITERATURE, IS THE MEDEVAC OR AERIAL MEDICAL TRANSPORT MARKET. ANOTHER POTENTIAL MVP IS THE USE OF NOVEL AIRCRAFT IN FERRY-LIKE SERVICES THAT OPERATE OVER SHORT RANGES ACROSS GEOGRAPHIC BOUNDARIES, SUCH AS BODIES OF WATER OR MOUNTAINS, TO OVERFLY CHOKE-POINTS IN CURRENT URBAN TRANSPORTATION NETWORKS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS TASK IS TO IDENTIFY MULTIPLE POTENTIAL MVPS FOR PASSENGER-CARRYING UAM OPERATIONS AND PERFORM ECONOMIC ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL VIABILITY OF AT LEAST ONE MVP. AN INITIAL ASSUMPTION IS THAT THERE IS NO UAM MVP IN EXISTENCE TODAY. THIS ASSUMPTION PRECLUDES THE ANALYSIS OF THIS TASK SUGGESTING THAT EXISTING CHARTER/PRIVATE HELICOPTER OPERATIONS (SUCH AS THOSE PERFORMED BY BLADE IN NEW YORK CITY) ARE A MVP. HOWEVER, EXTENSIONS OF THESE OPERATIONS INCLUDING ANALYSIS OF INCREASED MARKET SIZE WITH NOVEL TECHNOLOGIES (E.G., ELECTRIC VERTICAL TAKEOFF AND LANDING VEHICLES) COULD BE CONSIDERED A MVP. ADDITIONALLY, ALTHOUGH SOME COMPANIES ARE ELECTING TO EXPLORE NOVEL MARKETS OVERSEAS IN AREAS WITH DIFFERENCE REGULATORY ENVIRONMENTS, THIS EFFORT IS SOLELY FOCUSED ON INSTANTIATION OF POTENTIAL MARKETS IN THE U.S. OR ITS TERRITORIES.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: ANALYSIS OF OPERATIONAL ASPECTS OF ON DEMAND AIR MOBILITY: VERTIPORTS, AIRSPACE AND CONCEPTS.  THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF AEROSPACE (NIA), WORKING WITH THE MIT INTERNATIONAL CENTER FOR AIR TRANSPORTATION (ICAT), CONDUCTED PART I OF THE OPERATIONAL ASPECTS OF ON-DEMAND AIR MOBILITY STUDY FROM FEBRUARY 2016 THROUGH JULY 2017. THIS FIRST PART OF THE PROJECT COMPLETED A CASE STUDY IN LOS ANGELES TO IDENTIFY KEY SYSTEM-LEVEL CONSTRAINTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ON DEMAND MOBILITY (ODM) AVIATION SERVICES IN THE CONTEXT OF URBAN AIR MOBILITY (UAM). PART II OF THE STUDY, TITLED FURTHER ANALYSIS OF THE OPERATIONAL ASPECTS OF ON-DEMAND MOBILITY, WAS CONDUCTED FROM JULY 2017 TO JANUARY 2019. PART II EXPANDED THE CASE STUDY METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED IN PART I TO TWO ADDITIONAL CITIES, PRIORITIZED AND CHARACTERIZED THE SEVERITY OF THE IDENTIFIED OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINTS, AND DEVELOPED INITIAL MODELING TECHNIQUES FOR VERTIPORT OPERATIONS AND AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL. THIS WORK WAS PERFORMED UNDER NASA/NIA CONTRACT NO: NNL13AA08B; TASK ORDER NO: 80LARC17F0074.  THE INTENT OF THIS NEW TASK IS TO BUILD UPON THE FINDINGS AND OUTPUTS OF THE PART I AND II EFFORTS THROUGH A FOLLOW-ON STUDY. A PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS FOLLOW-ON WORK IS TO REFINE AND MATURE THE MODELS, TOOLS AND ANALYSIS METHODS DEVELOPED IN THE PREVIOUS PARTS OF THE PROJECT INTO A DOCUMENTED DELIVERABLE THAT CAN INFORM DEVELOPMENT OF THE NASA AIR TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT-EXPLORATION (ATM-X) TESTBED FOR USE IN SIMULATION ENVIRONMENTS AND STUDIES. FURTHERMORE, WHERE REQUESTED BY NASA, IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT THE CONTRACTOR WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF UAM CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS (CONOPS) AND TECHNOLOGY ROAD MAPPING THROUGH RESEARCH BRIEFS, TELECONFERENCES, AND PARTICIPATION IN MEETINGS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL INTERFACE WITH OTHER RESEARCH PROGRAMS, SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS, AND CONSULTANTS AS NECESSARY, FOR RESEARCH INTO SPECIFIC TOPICS THAT MAY ARISE.

THIS TASK PROVIDES FOR TECHNICAL SERVICES TO SUPPORT THE SUBSCALE FLIGHT RESEARCH LAB AND ITS RELATED PROJECTS AT THE NASA ARMSTRONG FLIGHT RESEARCH CENTER (AFRC). prime_award_base_transaction_description: MQ-9 (PREDATOR B) UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT.: IN 2006, NASA DRYDEN FLIGHT RESEARCH CENTER (DFRC) ACQUIRED A CIVILIANIZED VERSION OF THE MQ-9 PREDATOR B/REAPER UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEM (UAS) THAT WAS MODIFIED AND INSTRUMENTED FOR USE IN MULTIPLE CIVIL RESEARCH ROLES. THIS CONTRACT REQUIRES THE CONTRACTOR TO PROVIDE SUPPORT OF NASA S IKHANA UAS (NASA 870), WHICH INCLUDES THE AIRCRAFT (GA PART NUMBER UHK97000-3) AND THE GROUND CONTROL STATION (GA PART NUMBER SCD00545 REV B, S/N 3002) AND OTHER SUPPORT EQUIPMENT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT AND SUSTAIN FLIGHT RESEARCH AND FLIGHT OPERATIONS OF THE IKHANA. IN ADDITION, DFRC NEEDS OR MAY NEED THE CONTRACTOR S UNIQUE FACILITIES, SPECIALIZED TRAINING, UAS MAINTAINERS AND/OR AIRCREW PERSONNEL SUPPORT, SPARE PARTS, TOOLS, TECHNICAL DATA, SOFTWARE, TROUBLESHOOTING ANALYSES AND EVALUATIONS OF SYSTEM FAILURES, MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONS PROCEDURES AND/OR DRAWINGS USED IN THE AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE AND/OR DESIGN AND MANUFACTURE TO FACILITATE MODIFICATION OR REPAIR OF THE AIRCRAFT IN SUPPORT OF SPECIFIC IKHANA RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE INCLUDES REVIEWING PLANNED AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, PROVIDING DESIGN SUPPORT FOR UNIQUE CONTRACTOR SYSTEMS, AND ASSISTANCE IN DFRC PERFORMED ANALYSIS. THE CONTRACTOR MAY BE REQUIRED TO MODIFY OR TO PARTICIPATE/ASSIST IN THE MODIFICATION OF INTERNAL AIRCRAFT AVIONICS SYSTEMS, AIRCRAFT CONTROL SYSTEMS HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE, PERFORM AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, AND FABRICATE EXPERIMENTAL HARDWARE, WHERE THE INTIMATE KNOWLEDGE OF THE MANUFACTURED AIRCRAFT IS AN IMPORTANT FACTOR. DFRC MAY ALSO REQUEST RESEARCH STUDIES USING CONTRACTOR DEVELOPED MODELS AND SIMULATORS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUPPORT REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE THE INTEGRATION, MAINTENANCE, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE MODIFICATIONS TO THE IKHANA GCS AND GROUND DATA TERMINALS. TRAINING IN SUPPORT OF THE MQ-9 AND RELATED SUPPORT SYSTEMS SHALL BE PROVIDED BY THE CONTRACTOR. SUPPORT WILL PRIMARILY BE PROVIDED AT DFRC AND THE CONTRACTOR S FACILITIES, THOUGH THE NEEDS OF SOME TASKS MAY REQUIRE TRAVEL OR TEMPORARY DEPLOYMENT TO OTHER NASA CENTERS, CUSTOMER S FACILITIES, OR OTHER DOMESTIC OR FOREIGN OPERATIONAL DEPLOYMENT LOCATIONS.
